subject: health
essentialQuestion: How do I keep a disagreement from becoming a danger?

prompts.prompt: Explain assertive communication versus passive and aggressive patterns in your own words and give a valid example.
Use a cited source, diagram, model, or documented process to show understanding of de-escalation language and body positioning.
Apply conflict resolution and repair after a rupture in a new fictional situation. Show the decision process or cite the evidence used.
Analyze a plausible error, weak claim, or unsafe choice involving bullying, harassment, and hazing: recognition and reporting; correct it and explain why.
Connect warning signs of escalating violence and when to leave with reporting pathways and what happens after a report. Explain how the two support, constrain, or build on one another.

Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Take one fictional conflict from first friction to three different endings — repaired, disengaged, and reported — and justify which ending fits which conditions.
Identify one skill you can now transfer, one check that improves accuracy, and one next question.

adaptationChoices: Branching may be diagrammed, written, narrated, or completed on a supplied decision-tree template. Verbal rehearsal is optional and never public.
accommodationNote: Access supports may change format, pacing, quantity, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. No assessment requires disclosure, a recording, or any body measurement.
trustedAdultNote: Direct any urgent safety, health, or mental-health concern to a trusted adult or qualified professional; this course is not diagnosis, therapy, or treatment.
neverRequires: This task never requires body weight, height, BMI, or body-fat percentage.
This task never requires calorie counting or a diet or weight-loss goal.
This task never requires disclosing private medical history, a diagnosis, or sexual history.
This task never requires a photograph, video, or voice recording of the learner as proof.
This task never requires a public performance or an audience.
